hold_text: Edits .github/actions/commit-to-main/action.yml, which R12's own LANDING_MACHINERY list names as a THIRD landing route -- it writes the pr-landing declaration, the arming file and the R13 merge-slot claim, and calls `gh pr merge --auto --squash` for all 27 workflows that use it. R12 is exactly right to hold this: the change and its own approval would otherwise be the same act, and a mistake in it disarms the check that would have caught the mistake. I have NOT weakened, excepted or marked R12, and there is no automerge request file. WHAT A HUMAN SHOULD ACTUALLY CHECK, because it is one property and not the whole diff: that the recompute can never resolve a file the caller does not own. Three conditions are ANDed and all three are load-bearing -- (1) a `refresh-command` is declared, so the caller has stated it can recompute its own output; (2) EVERY conflicted path is one the caller named in `paths:`, computed into UNDECLARED before any branch is taken, so one path outside that list aborts exactly as today; (3) the recompute exits 0. The blast radius is therefore bounded by the caller's own `paths:` list, which is an explicit caller-supplied enumeration and never a wildcard -- the same invariant the `-f` comment already in this action exists to protect. The second condition is the one worth reading closely, because it is what separates 'recompute my own generated artifact' from 'resolve somebody else's data', and the replay confirms it fires: 3 of 33 real branches were REFUSED by it for conflicting on docs/claude/session-board.json. Also worth a look: main's side is taken first (`git checkout --theirs -- ${CONFLICTED}`) before the recompute, so nothing already on main is lost and any declared path the command does not rewrite keeps main's content. A mutation flipping that to `--ours` initially PASSED the suite -- a bare `"--theirs" in s` was satisfied by the unrelated session-board block above it -- and the test now pins the exact line. ⚠️ NOTHING HERE TOUCHES AN ORDER PATH, config, deploy, or any env knob; the diff is one composite action, three workflow `with:` blocks, and one test file.
why: MEASURED 2026-09-17 at origin/main 19e59662, population = EVERY open PR (all 70, both API pages), probed with `git merge-tree --write-tree` on an unshallowed clone with BOTH controls passing (positive: a whole-file rewrite off an old commit -> conflicted rc=1; negative: main vs main -> clean): 56 of 70 open PRs (80.0%) are merge-conflicted, 44 of them `automation/**` -- this action's OWN PRs -- and ZERO anywhere in src/, tests/, scripts/ or config/. The blocked paths are led by GENERATED files: DUE.json/DUE.md in 28 PRs, ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.json/.md in 23, with 23 error-feed-digest PRs stacked up since 2026-09-13 -- an hourly run conflicting with every earlier unmerged run OF ITSELF. A generated artifact has no side to take; its content is a pure function of its inputs, so the correct merge is to RECOMPUTE it. The action's `refresh-command` was already that remedy and was unreachable in the one case that needed it: it sits in the merge-SUCCEEDED arm, so a merge that CONFLICTED hit `git merge --abort` first and stranded the branch. It was also barely used -- 1 of 27 call sites set it against 27 of 27 setting `verify-merged`, the latter being the positive control that the probe can see a real input. THE OBSERVATION, which is what makes this more than a self-test: replayed against the 33 REAL stranded automation branches on origin -- reproduce the actual `git merge origin/main`, apply the new resolution, re-probe -- 30 go CONFLICT -> CLEAN and 3 are correctly refused. `paths:` and the recompute command are parsed from the workflow files themselves, because v1 of the replay transcribed them by hand, mis-copied two, and produced 11 spurious aborts that were my error and not the fix. The new guard in tests/test_commit_to_main_callers.py (a caller that lands an artifact it generates in-job must declare a `refresh-command`) immediately found a 4th caller I had not identified, sunset-pass, which is exempted because it writes comms/sunset/<UTC-date>/ -- disjoint per run, verified on disk -- with the exemption VERIFIED rather than presence-only. 6 of 6 realistic mutations are caught, including two that initially passed and are recorded in the evidence doc because the reasoning behind each looked sound. Full census, replay table and the research/testing/ML infra verdict: docs/claude/work/REGISTER-CONTENTION-AND-RESEARCH-INFRA-2026-09-17.md. NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: the replay-pregate R5/runtime_logs blocker (separate concern, filed as BL-20260917-PR-LANDING-R5-REFUSES-RUNTIME-LOGS-SO-REPLAY-PREGATE-CAN-NEVER-LAND-A-REPORT-EVEN-IF-IT-FINISHES), the 12 conflicted substantive PRs (each needs its author's judgement on a register union), and anything Tier-2/3.
